subject.title: Feature: Agent 动态切换命令（不重启 Gateway）

question: Should OpenClaw add a channel-level `/agent <id>` configured-agent switch, and what authorization/state boundary should control which channel senders may target which agents?
rationale: The requested UX changes who owns an active chat, workspace, credentials, tools, memory, and transcript state; source inspection shows no existing policy that safely answers that for channel senders.

options.title: Design guarded core switch
options.body: Define an opt-in core conversation-routing command that reuses or extends an explicit allow policy, stores durable per-conversation state, and ships docs plus route/security tests.

options.title: Limit to existing subagent controls
options.body: Keep `/focus`, `/unfocus`, `/agents`, and `sessions_spawn` as the supported dynamic routing path and decline configured-agent chat switching for now.

options.title: Defer to broader routing RFC
options.body: Leave this issue open as input to a broader multi-agent routing design instead of implementing a one-off command surface.

recommendation.title: Design guarded core switch
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in core conversation-routing command that reuses or extends an explicit allow policy, stores durable per-conversation state, and ships docs plus route/security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent route resolver, command registry, and conversation binding history make this the strongest available routing/security decision owner from the inspected history.
